newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S LEU SLIGHTLY DOWN, MONEY MARKET RATES UP.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S LEU SLIGHTLY DOWN, MONEY MARKET RATES UP.

text.p: 1310 GMT - Romania's leu ended slightly weaker at about 7,400/440 to the dollar on Wednesday against opening quotes of 7,360/475 in a quiet interbank market, traders said.
But leu-dollar rates remained firmer than Tuesday's close of about 7,410/495.
* Operators said dollar demand had been low in recent days with most importers on the sidelines due to the summer period. This helped the leu to gain some ground, they said.
* Dealers said new norms on foreign investment repatriation announced by the central bank (BNR) late on Wednesday had no immediate impact on the market.
Some operators said the new norms, expected to put an end to procedural hurdles for portfolio repatriation, were unlikely to trigger large foreign capital outflows in the near future.
"The T-bills market is attractive. For the time being, portfolio investors might refrain from testing the new norms as there was an upswing in yields," a dealer said.
* Six-month T-bill yield inched up to an annual 55.01 percent at Wednesday's auction from a previous 54.99 percent, with banks' bids double the finance ministry offer.
Traders said the rise would continue to drag up short-term money market rates which closed Wednesday higher at around 35 percent on overnight funds and near 45 percent for one-week.
Some operators expected short-term prices to open even higher on Thursday at around 38 percent on overnight and 47 percent for one-week funds.
* Leu-dollar retail prices hovered at about 7,300/500.
